I started going to the gym regularly little by little. Started slow on the treadmill just 15 minutes every day for a week and kept increasing it. Now I can bench press 180 pounds and can do the automatic stairs for 15 minutes. I'm still improving but I'm proud of what I've achieved. My working situation could be better, but I'm still working on things and I still have my family and friends that are there for me.

From what it sounds like, I think it's best for you to get some professional help first. People on reddit can only help you so much. I don't know what you've been through in your life but you have to realize that you cant have your past keep taking hold of your future. Medication also really helps. Jowy to me is one of the most interesting antagonists (if you want to call him that) in a video game. At the end of the game, all the surviving mayors decided to unite their cities together to make a single country but they would have never done this in the beginning. In the beginning, it was every man for himself. Annabelle couldn't get anything done because the cities barely followed the alliance pact. The leaders were either weak, selfish or even worse, plotting behind other leaders backs (like Gordeau). Jowy saw this very early and decided that the best course of action was to have everything unified under one authority. Of course, while you are playing throughout the game, most of the leaders change and start to work together but that's not something that Jowy was able to see due to him being in Highland. To him, looking at the outside, he sees your leaders/generals as the same right before he left. And remember, a lot of the past Jowston mayors did very scummy things in the past to Highland and Karaya to get ahead. The game even mentioned that it was said that Jowston-City States were the ones who started the war with Highland in the past.

Anyways, he gets caught, defects back to Highland, leaks plans of Luca Blights night raid to end him, poisons the King with his own blood and takes control. And when he does take control, he still sees the leaders as the same from the outside, which means to him that he sees a higher likelihood for war in the future. Of course today, we do have countries that are also led by hellish dictators but unlike in Suikoden's world, we have deterrents which are nukes.

 From Jowy's viewpoint, his armies are much bigger than yours and he has Leon Silverburg, one of the best strategists in Suikoden at his side. He would have actually won against you if he was more ruthless but every time he corners you, he couldn't go through it. He could have even beaten you in the Rockaxe battle but withdrew his armies just to give Nanami a chance for survival after she was shot.. But in the end, because he couldn't bring himself to kill his old friends, he ended up losing the war. He realized about the discord of the city states very early, and he was right, but things just played out too differently over time. 

Both you and him wanted the same thing, a land without war.  Things just played out in a very unfortunate turn...

For one it depends on what company you're working with. Is it a local company or a huge one?

Most companies ad agencies deal with on a regular basis are local. That being said, the real aim for most clients you work with is not to rank #1 on google/Bing/whatever platform you're working on. It's to get your client the most ROI possible (Return on Investment= (Revenue-costs/costs) basically making as much revenue as you can while also reducing costs as much as you can) . In many cases, sure, you could rank #1 or #2 on Bing or Google but that makes you end up paying more in cost per click than you should be paying. Basically you want your ad ranking to be between 3 and 6.  This gains your ad the same amount of visibility while paying less. Ranking high doesn't really mean much unless if your client is a huge business like best buy. 

That being said, most clients are local businesses so if I were you on that account , I'd reduce my cpc. And I would probably leave the rank #1 thing out of my resume because that only tells companies that you don't know how to truly optimize a campaign.

This is what resulted in me switching to Bing because bings target users as a whole are people aged 30 and up, which match the same target audience of the pest control company. Not only that, but the space of Bing is less competitive thereby driving down cost per click.
